subject: Clarifying controller/processor roles, telemetry & embeddings — DPA redline and signing path
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightleaf.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Cc: BrightLeaf Analytics Legal <legal@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Initial DPA redline + questions on embeddings / telemetry retention

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. We did a quick review and flagged a few areas we need clarified before we can proceed to signature:

1) Roles: the DPA currently lists Redwood as "processor" but the definitions for "embeddings" and exported vectors are ambiguous. BrightLeaf will be the controller of customer inputs and derived embeddings for our product — we need assurance on access, export, and deletion timelines for vectors.

2) Telemetry & logs: your redline allows telemetry retention up to 24 months for operational metrics. We need scoped telemetry agreement — e.g., operational metrics (latency, error rates) vs. request-level logs or partial KV cache snapshots. Request-level logs containing PII must be excluded or pseudonymized.

3) Subprocessors: please provide your current list (including cloud providers used for vector storage/replication) and confirm notification cadence for new subprocessors.

4) Cross-border transfer: we prefer SCCs or an equivalent UK addendum for transfers outside the EEA. Please confirm whether you can supply SCCs or rely on UK addendum flow.

Attached is our annotated redline (BrightLeaf_DPA_Redline_v2.docx) and a short summary of the must-haves. Can you confirm which items are deal blockers vs. negotiable? Also please send the preferred DocuSign/AdobeSign contact for execution.

Best,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Legal Operations
BrightLeaf Analytics

--
Attachment: BrightLeaf_DPA_Redline_v2.docx (document with inline comments)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.inference, irene_choi@redwood.inference
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + questions on embeddings / telemetry retention

Hi Sarah — thanks for the detailed notes and the annotated redline. Looping in Laura (legal) and Irene (privacy/ops) to align quickly.

High level: we want to be as narrow as possible on controller/processor language while keeping the platform usable for customers. A few quick positions from product/ops:
- Embeddings: Redwood treats model outputs (including embedding vectors) as derived data from customer inputs. By default we operate as processor for storage and serving of those vectors, but we can add explicit language that BrightLeaf retains controller rights over label/meaning and can request export/deletion on demand within x days.
- Telemetry: we can split telemetry into (a) aggregated operational metrics (retained 24 months by default) and (b) request-level diagnostic logs / traces (retained 30 days, can be reduced or pseudonymized on request). We do not retain raw customer prompt text in diagnostic logs by default — that can be redacted or token-hashed per the DPA.
- Subprocessors: attached is the current subprocessors CSV and cloud-region mapping. We have a 30-day notification for material subcontractor changes.

Irene/Laura — can you review the attached and propose specific wording (controller v processor table + deletion SLAs) so I can route to the customer? Also Sarah — please flag anything that is a firm requirement for your compliance team vs. something you can take via an ops workaround (e.g., pseudonymization instead of deletion for certain debug logs).

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Business Development, Redwood Inference
phone: +1-415-555-0124

Attachments: subprocessors-2027-01.csv, redline-summary-20270114.txt

From: laura_bennett@redwood.inference <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightleaf.ai>, irene_choi@redwood.inference
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + questions on embeddings / telemetry retention

Vivek / Sarah — I reviewed BrightLeaf's annotated redline and drafted a short mapping table to make roles explicit. Summary below (keeping it short for email):

Proposed mapping (editable for final DPA):
- Controller: BrightLeaf Analytics (controls input data and determines processing purposes).
- Processor: Redwood Inference (processes inputs to produce model outputs, stores vectors, operates serving runtime).
- Joint responsibilities: When Redwood enriches telemetry or aggregates embeddings for platform performance research, we will ensure data is aggregated and cannot be re-linked to a controller without consent.

Key redlines I propose to accept / counter:
1) Embeddings export/delete SLA: Acceptable counter — Redwood will export or delete customer embeddings on written request within 7 business days for standard export/deletion; for bulk archival we can extend to 14 calendar days with notice.
2) Telemetry retention split: Accept the separation — operational metrics 24 months; request-level diagnostic logs 30 days default. We will add pseudonymization option in the appendix with a 30-day retention unless a customer requests shorter.
3) Subprocessors: Provide full list (attached). We will commit to 30-day notice and allow a limited termination right if a new subprocessor materially impacts BrightLeaf's compliance posture.
4) Cross-border transfers: We can execute SCCs for EEA transfers and support the UK addendum. Will include a DPA exhibit with transfer mechanisms.

I've attached a redline summary (redline-summary-20270114.txt) and a short DPA mark showing the controller/processor table. If BrightLeaf can confirm the export/delete SLA and telemetry pseudonymization option, we can prepare the DocuSign envelope.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline-summary-20270114.txt

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightleaf.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.inference, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 10:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + questions on embeddings / telemetry retention

Laura / Vivek — thanks for the quick turnaround and the mapping table. We reviewed internally with our GTM and security teams; a few follow-ups before we finalize:

- Embeddings SLA: 7 business days for export/deletion is reasonable. For the record, we'll request a one-time bulk export as part of our onboarding so we can validate.
- Telemetry: the split is acceptable but want confirmation that request-level logs will never include full prompt text for PII-sensitive customers. Token-hashing or redaction is fine.
- Subprocessors: two clarifying questions on the CSV — which region hosts the vector replica (US vs EU)? Also please confirm whether any subprocessors have access to raw request bodies for debugging.
- Execution: BrightLeaf prefers DocuSign. Can Redwood set up the envelope and list our legal ops contact as signatory (Sarah Nguyen)? Please include the DPA exhibit for cross-border transfers and the SCCs/UK addendum as attachments in the envelope.

If you can confirm the points above we can circle back and sign next week.

Thanks,
Sarah

--
Quick inline: we will take the pseudonymization option for debug logs; confirm replication region and debug access and we can proceed.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.inference, irene_choi@redwood.inference
Date: Sun, 17 Jan 2027 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + questions on embeddings / telemetry retention

Sarah — thanks, all good. Final confirmations:

- Embeddings export/delete: Redwood confirms 7 business days for standard export/deletion requests. We will schedule your onboarding bulk export; I'll coordinate with our infra team on timing.
- Telemetry: request-level logs will not include full prompt text for PII-sensitive tenants by default. We'll apply token-hashing/redaction. The pseudonymization appendix will be included in the DPA exhibit.
- Subprocessors & regions: the attached CSV indicates vector replicas can be hosted in US, EU, or APAC depending on customer selection; for BrightLeaf we can lock replicas to the US or EU — please confirm region preference before signing. No subprocessors have unrestricted access to raw request bodies; access is role-based and audited.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood will attach SCCs and the UK addendum in the DocuSign envelope.

I will prepare the DocuSign envelope and include: (1) final redline v3, (2) SCCs & UK addendum exhibit, (3) subprocessors CSV, (4) pseudonymization appendix. Envelope link below — please confirm signatory and region preference and we'll send.

DocuSign envelope (draft): https://docusign.net/envelope/EXAMPLE-ENVELOPE-ID-12345

Next steps: Sarah confirms signatory + region, BrightLeaf signs via DocuSign, legal executes and we send onboarding runbook for bulk export. Target window to sign: next week (w/c 2027-01-25).

Best,
Vivek
Head of Business Development
Redwood Inference
phone: +1-415-555-0124

Attachments included in envelope: BrightLeaf_DPA_Redline_v3.docx, SCCs-EEA.pdf, UK-Addendum.pdf, subprocessors-2027-01.csv, pseudonymization-appendix.pdf
